basketball#Retired numbers|retired by Washington Huskies]] * [[Washington Huskies]] Athletics Hall of Fame (2023) }} '''Isaiah Jamar Thomas''' (born February 7, 1989) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who is working as a [[NBA scout|scout]] for the [[Boston Celtics]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He is best known for playing with the Celtics from [[2015–16 NBA season|2015]] through [[2016–17 NBA season|2017]], where he was a two-time [[NBA All-Star]] and named second-team [[All-NBA]]. The {{convert|5|ft|9|in|adj=on}} [[point guard]] played three years of [[college basketball]] for the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington Huskies]] and was a three-time [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] selection in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-10]]. After electing to forgo his senior year of college, Thomas was selected by the [[Sacramento Kings]] with the final pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]]. He spent three seasons with the Kings before joining the [[Phoenix Suns]] in 2014. Thomas was traded to Boston in February 2015. In the 2016–17 season, he led the Celtics to the first seed of the [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]], had the third-highest points-per-game average in the league, and finished fifth in [[NBA Most Valuable Player Award|MVP]] voting. After injuring his right hip during the 2016–17 season, Thomas was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in August 2017. Over the next several seasons, his hip injury significantly hampered his play. Thomas went on to play for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], [[Denver Nuggets]], [[Washington Wizards]], [[New Orleans Pelicans]], [[Dallas Mavericks]], [[Charlotte Hornets]], and Suns again, along with several stints in the NBA G League. ==Early life== Isaiah Thomas was born on February 7, 1989{{Cite web|url=https://www.wkyc.com/article/sports/nba/cavaliers/whos-isaiah-thomas-meet-the-cleveland-cavaliers-new-star-point-guard/95-466700093|title=Who's Isaiah Thomas? He was named [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Pac-10 Freshman of the Year]] and second-team [[All-Pac-10 men's basketball team|All-Pac-10]]. As a sophomore, Thomas' averages rose to 16.9 points, 3.2 assists, and 3.9 rebounds per game. He was named first-team All-Pac-10.{{cite web|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=208063595&DB_OEM_ID=30200|title=Isaiah Thomas Biography|work=GoHuskies.com|access-date=April 13, 2016|archive-date=March 3, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303175319/http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30200&ATCLID=208063595|url-status=dead}} Thomas was again named first-team All-Pac-10 in his junior year. On March 12, 2011, Thomas scored 28 points and hit a game-winning buzzer beater in overtime to lead the Huskies to victory over Arizona in the championship game of the Pac-10 tournament. He was among the final ten candidates for the [[Bob Cousy Award]] in his junior season.{{cite web|url=http://www.cousyaward.com/docs/CousyAward2011.pdf |title=BASKETBALL HALL OF FAME ANNOUNCES FINAL TEN CANDIDATES FOR 2011 BOB COUSY AWARD |work=[[Bob Cousy Award]] |date=February 7, 2011 |access-date=July 7, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111002104704/http://www.cousyaward.com/docs/CousyAward2011.pdf |archive-date=October 2, 2011 }} A few weeks later on March 31, Thomas declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final year of college eligibility.{{cite web |url= http://latimesblogs.latimes.com/sports_blog/2011/03/pac-10-basketball-washington-star-guard-isaiah-thomas-declares-for-nba-draft.html|title=Sports Now| work= Los Angeles Times|date=March 31, 2011|access-date=April 13, 2016}} ==Professional career== ===Sacramento Kings (2011–2014)=== [[File:Isaiah Thomas Dec 2013.jpg|thumb|Thomas in 2013]] Before the 2011 NBA draft, Thomas participated in his own pre-draft documentary entitled "Road to the NBA–The Isaiah Thomas Story".{{cite web |url= http://seattletimes.nwsource.com/html/huskymensbasketballblog/2015392991_road_to_the_nba.html |title=Husky Men's Basketball Blog | Road to the NBA – The Isaiah Thomas Story|work=The Seattle Times|access-date=June 23, 2011| first= Percy| last= Allen|date=June 22, 2011}} Thomas was selected in the second round of the [[2011 NBA draft]] with the 60th and final pick by the [[Sacramento Kings]]. On February 19, 2012, he recorded his first double-double with 23 points and 11 assists against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/320219005|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230220020018/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/320219005|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 20, 2023|title=Kyrie Irving's two free throws with 0.4 seconds left lift Cavs|work=ESPN|agency=Associated Press|date=February 19, 2012|access-date=February 20, 2023|location=Cleveland}} On March 1, 2012, Thomas was named the Western Conference [[NBA Rookie of the Month]] after averaging 12.2 points and 4.4 assists per contest in February.{{cite web |url= http://www.nba.com/kings/news/isaiah_thomas_rookie_of_the_month_release.html |title= Cleveland's Kyrie Irving and Sacramento's Isaiah Thomas Named Rookies of the Month |website= [[NBA.com]] |access-date=March 1, 2012|date=March 1, 2012}} No player before had gone on to win Rookie of the Month honors after being picked last in the NBA draft. On December 16, 2015, Thomas tied his then-career high of 38 points in a 119–116 loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151216/BOSDET/gameinfo.html|title=Caldwell-Pope scores 31 points, Pistons beat Celtics 119–116|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=December 16, 2015|access-date=December 16, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170622004936/http://www.nba.com/games/20151216/BOSDET/gameinfo.html|archive-date=June 22, 2017|url-status=dead}} On January 28, 2016, Thomas was named an Eastern Conference All-Star reserve for the [[2016 NBA All-Star Game]].{{cite web|last=D'Amico|first=Marc|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/sidebar/012816-no-debate-isaiah-thomas-is-an-all-star|title=No Debate: Isaiah Thomas is an All-Star|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=January 28, 2016|access-date=January 28, 2016}} He became the lowest draft pick to be named an All-Star since the NBA draft was reduced to two rounds in 1989. Thomas also became only the ninth player under {{convert|6|ft}} to be named an All-Star, while also tying [[Calvin Murphy]] as the shortest player to be selected for the All-Star Game.{{cite web|last=Forsberg|first=Chris|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/celtics/post/_/id/4721841/isaiah-thomas-on-potential-all-star-nod-i-feel-like-i-deserve-it|title=Celtics guard Isaiah Thomas earns first All-Star nod|publisher=ESPN|date=January 29, 2016|access-date=January 29, 2016}} On February 8, 2016, Thomas was named Eastern Conference Player of the Week for games played Monday, February 1, through Sunday, February 7.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/020816-Isaiah-Thomas-Named-Eastern-Conference-Player-of-the-Week|title=Thomas Named Eastern Conference Player of the Week|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=February 8, 2016|access-date=February 8, 2016}} With the Celtics down 2–0 to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in the first round of the 2016 playoffs, Thomas scored a then-career-high 42 points in Game 3 in Boston to lift the Celtics to a 111–103 victory. He became only the ninth Celtic to score 40 points in a playoff game.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160422/ATLBOS/gameinfo.html|title=Thomas scores 42, lifts Celtics over Hawks 111–103 in Game 3|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=April 22, 2016|access-date=April 22, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170529204327/http://www.nba.com/games/20160422/ATLBOS/gameinfo.html|archive-date=May 29, 2017|url-status=dead}} With 28 points in Game 4, Thomas helped the Celtics even the series at 2–2 with a 104–95 overtime victory.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160424/ATLBOS/gameinfo.html|title=Celtics beat Hawks 104–95 in OT, series tied 2–2|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=April 24, 2016|access-date=April 25, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180428121014/http://www.nba.com/games/20160424/ATLBOS/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 28, 2018|url-status=dead}} However, the Celtics went on to lose the series in six games.{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/400874416|title=Hawks hand Celtics their third straight first-round playoff exit|work=ESPN|agency=Associated Press|location=Boston|date=April 29, 2016|access-date=February 20, 2023}} [[File:Isaiah Thomas (34300573362).jpg|thumb|right|Thomas in 2017]] Thomas scored 20 or more points in 20 of the first 21 games of the 2016–2017 season.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/thomais02/gamelog/2017/|title=Isaiah Thomas 2016–17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=February 4, 2017}} He was injured in a December 5, 2016, game against the Houston Rockets and received a platelet-rich plasma injection. After returning from a four-game absence for what the Celtics described as a groin strain,{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/20595342/nba-cleveland-cavaliers-guard-isaiah-thomas-faces-uncertain-return-potentially-career-ending-hip-injury|title=For better or worse, LeBron James and Isaiah Thomas are now joined at Thomas' fragile hip|date=September 5, 2017|website=ESPN.com}} Thomas continued to put up big numbers.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899833|title=Thomas scores 26 points to lead Celtics over Hornets, 96–88|publisher=ESPN|date=December 16, 2016|access-date=December 17, 2016}} On December 20, he scored a then-career-high 44 points in a 112–109 overtime victory over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. He also matched his career best for three-pointers, going 7-of-10 from outside the arc.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899866|title=Thomas scores career-high 44, Celtics beat Grizzlies in OT|publisher=ESPN|date=December 20, 2016|access-date=December 21, 2016}} Thomas earned Eastern Conference Player of the Week honors for the week spanning December 19 through December 25.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2016/12/26/nba-players-week-isaiah-thomas-russell-westbrook|title=Isaiah Thomas, Russell Westbrook named Players of the Week|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=December 26, 2016|access-date=December 30, 2016}} On December 30 against the [[Miami Heat]], he scored 29 of his career-high 52 points in the fourth quarter, setting a franchise record for points in a period and leading Boston to a 117–114 victory.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899936|title=Thomas scores 52 for Celtics in 117–114 win over Miami|publisher=ESPN|date=December 30, 2016|access-date=December 30, 2016}} Thomas' 52 points was the fourth-highest scoring total in Celtics history—[[Larry Bird]] holds the record, having scored 60 points in March 1985 game. On January 3, 2017, Thomas recorded 29 points and a career-high 15 assists in a 115–104 victory over the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899423|title=Thomas' 29 points, 15 assists send Celtics past Jazz 115–104|publisher=ESPN|date=January 3, 2017|access-date=January 4, 2017}} On January 26, 2017, Thomas was named an Eastern Conference All-Star reserve for the [[2017 NBA All-Star Game]].{{cite web|last=Whitaker|first=Lang|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/01/26/nba-all-star-reserves-2017-revealed|title=Warriors, Cavaliers dominate selections for NBA All-Star 2017 as reserves are revealed|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=January 26, 2017|access-date=January 27, 2017}} He averaged 32.9 points in January, marking the third-highest monthly average in team history.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900142|title=Thomas scores 41 for Celtics in 113–109 win over Pistons|publisher=ESPN|date=January 30, 2017|access-date=January 31, 2017}} On February 2, Thomas was named Eastern Conference Player of the Month for January. He led the NBA in scoring (32.9 ppg) and tied for fifth in the East in assists (6.9 apg) for the month as the Celtics went 10–4 to take over first place in the Atlantic Division.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/02/02/isaiah-thomas-stephen-curry-kevin-durant-named-players-month-january|title=Thomas, Curry and Durant named players of month for January|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=February 2, 2017|access-date=February 2, 2017}} On February 15, Thomas scored 33 points in a 116–108 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. It was his 40th straight 20-point game, tying a team record set by [[John Havlicek]] during the 1971–72 season.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900242|title=Thomas scores 33, Celtics hold off late push by 76ers|publisher=ESPN|date=February 15, 2017|access-date=February 15, 2017}} The following day, Thomas broke Havlicek's team record with a 41st straight 20-point game; he scored 29 points in a 104–103 loss to the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900255|title=Butler lifts Bulls to 104–103 victory over Celtics|publisher=ESPN|date=February 16, 2017|access-date=February 17, 2017}} With 19 points against the [[Atlanta Hawks]] on February 27, Thomas' franchise-record streak of consecutive 20-point games ended at 43. It was only the second time during the season that he did not score at least 20 points in a game.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900291|title=Hawks prevail 114–98 in scrappy showdown with Celtics|publisher=ESPN|date=February 27, 2017|access-date=February 27, 2017}} Thomas suffered an injury in a March 15, 2017, game against the Minnesota Timberwolves and missed the following two games. With 32 points against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] on March 29, he became only the sixth Celtic ever to score 2,000 points in a single season. Thomas also extended his streak with at least one three-pointer to a franchise-best 50 straight games.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900508|title=Bucks fend off late Celtics rally in 103–100 win|publisher=ESPN|date=March 29, 2017|access-date=March 30, 2017}} Behind his leadership, the Celtics finished the 2016–2017 season as the top seed in the Eastern Conference;{{Cite web|url=https://fansided.com/2021/09/17/isaiah-thomas-last-chance-workout-warriors/|title=Isaiah Thomas is getting a last-chance workout with the Warriors|website=Fansided.com|date=September 17, 2021}}{{cite web|url=https://kgmi.com/news/007700-nba-playoffs-former-husky-isaiah-thomas-leads-celtics-to-no-1-seed-in-the-eastern-conference/|title=NBA Playoffs: Former Husky Isaiah Thomas leads Celtics to No. 1 seed in the Eastern Conference |website=KGMI.com |date=April 13, 2017 }} the team's record was 53–29.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/BOS/2017.html|title=2016–17 Boston Celtics Roster and Stats|website=Basketball-Reference.com}} Thomas finished the regular season as the third-leading scorer in the NBA, averaging 28.9 points per game.{{Cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10004000-isaiah-thomas-says-celtics-didnt-reveal-long-term-risk-of-2017-hip-injury|title=Isaiah Thomas Says Celtics Didn't Reveal Long-term Risk of 2017 Hip Injury|first=Rob|last=Goldberg|website=Bleacher Report}} [[File:Isaiah Thomas (34363102672).jpg|thumb|right|Thomas drives to the basket in the 2017 playoffs]] In the 2017 playoffs, Thomas led the Celtics to a first-round series victory over the Chicago Bulls after learning the day before the series began that his younger sister, Chyna, had died in a car accident. This was the Celtics first playoff series win in five years. After the Celtics defeated the Bulls in six games, Thomas flew cross-country to attend his sister's funeral. Thomas returned to Boston for Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals and helped the Celtics defeat the [[Washington Wizards]] 123–111.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400952526|title=Thomas' 33, Celtics' 3s too much for Wizards in 123–111 win|publisher=ESPN|date=April 30, 2017|access-date=April 30, 2017}} According to ESPN, during Game 1, "Thomas lost a front tooth following an inadvertent elbow from Otto Porter, requiring surgery to replace it and fix two other shifted teeth. He played through the dental wreck and scored 33 points and notched nine assists in the win. He didn't miss a game". Two days later in Game 2, Thomas scored 53 points—the second-highest total in Celtics playoff history—to help Boston win 129–119 in overtime and take a 2–0 lead in the series. He became only the fifth Celtic to score 50 or more points in a postseason game, missing John Havlicek's team record by one point.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400952527|title=Thomas scores 53, Celtics beat Wizards 129–119 in OT|publisher=ESPN|date=May 2, 2017|access-date=May 2, 2017}} In Game 7, Thomas scored 29 points and had 12 assists to help the Celtics advance to the Eastern Conference Finals for the first time since 2012 with a 115–105 victory.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400952532|title=Celtics power past Wizards in Game 7, 115–105|publisher=ESPN|date=May 15, 2017|access-date=May 15, 2017}} After the Celtics lost the first two games of the 2017 Eastern Conference Finals to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], Thomas was ruled out for the rest of the postseason with a hip injury.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press-052017-isaiah-thomas-ruled-out-for-game-3|title=Isaiah Thomas Ruled Out for Remainder of Playoffs|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=May 20, 2017|access-date=May 20, 2017}} In a statement, the Celtics said:
Isaiah Thomas will miss the remainder of this year's postseason following re-aggravation of a right femoral-acetabular impingement with labral tear during Game 2 of the Eastern Conference Finals against Cleveland. Thomas initially injured the hip during the third quarter of the Celtics' March 15 game against Minnesota... the injury was further aggravated during Game 6 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals at Washington on May 12.

[[File:Isaiah Thomas free throw (cropped).jpg|thumb|Thomas shoots a free throw in 2020]] ===Washington Wizards (2019–2020)=== On July 10, 2019, Thomas signed with the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-sign-isaiah-thomas|title=Wizards sign Isaiah Thomas|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=July 10, 2019}} He injured his left thumb on September 16 and underwent surgery on two days later.{{Cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2019/09/18/wizards-isaiah-thomas-out-6-8-weeks-after-thumb-surgery/40166981/|title=Wizards' Isaiah Thomas out 6–8 weeks after thumb surgery|website=USA TODAY}} On December 22, Thomas was suspended for two games without pay for entering the stands during a game.{{Cite web|title=Wizards' Isaiah Thomas suspended|date=December 23, 2019|url=https://pr.nba.com/isaiah-thomas-suspension-washington-wizards/|access-date=October 11, 2021|publisher=National Basketball Association}} In 40 games with the Wizards, he averaged 12.2 points per game on 40.8% shooting and 41.3% shooting from beyond the three-point arc.
